about: Successive CDC/CSTE surveillance case definitions for Lyme disease, as versions. Each version is named by CDC for the year it is used from; 'effective' is January 1 of that year (surveillance years follow MMWR weeks, which start within a few days of January 1). 'announced' is when CSTE adopted the position statement behind it; only the year can be read from the statement number, so it is given as a year and counts as known only once that year has ended, except where CDC gives a season. Versions before 2011 (1995, 1996, 2008) exist but are not in this graph yet. Checked on 2026-10-14 against CDC's NNDSS case definition pages. Research data, not medical advice.

versions.note: CDC dates position statement 21-ID-05 to spring 2021. It is given as June 2021, the last month of spring, so it is never treated as known too early. The 2022 definition classifies cases differently in high- and low-incidence jurisdictions.
